Summary Trevor Noah, the renowned comedian and former host of The Daily Show, recently visited Malaysian Prime Minister Datuk Seri Anwar Ibrahim, receiving unexpected comedic advice ahead of his performance in Kuala Lumpur.
 The interaction between Noah and Anwar was filled with humor and discussions on politics and comedy, with Anwar playfully offering to crowdfund a rescue if Noah's jokes caused any trouble.
 Noah's Malaysian shows, part of his 2026 Asia tour, have seen significant success, selling out both performances.
 Make Malay Mail your preferred source on Google Giving you news that matter to Malaysians. Make Malay Mail your preferred source when you search for news on Google. By Malay Mail First Published: Tuesday, 10 Nov 2026 4:51 PM MYT × Subscribe to Newsletter
 Subscribe KUALA LUMPUR, Nov 10 — Trevor Noah has received some last-minute comedy advice from an unlikely source — Prime Minister Datuk Seri Anwar Ibrahim, who joked about crowdfunding a rescue if the comedian’s punchlines get him into trouble.
 The South African stand-up star and former The Daily Show host paid a visit to Anwar today, with the two swapping stories about politics, humour and just about everything in between.
 And judging by Anwar’s Facebook post, there was plenty of laughter.
 “It was a pleasure to welcome Trevor Noah today. We had the chance to chat about politics, humour and all sorts of other things, with plenty of laughter along the way,” Anwar wrote.
 The prime minister also revealed that he had offered Noah a few pointers on what might — or might not — go down well on stage.
 “I also managed to share a few pointers on the kind of jokes he could bring to the stage tonight. Hopefully, no one takes offence!” he quipped.
 But Anwar saved his best punchline for last.
 “Anyway, don’t worry, Trevor. If anything happens tonight, we’ll all chip in and crowdfund together!” he added, signing off with laughing emojis.
 The playful exchange comes as Noah prepares to wrap up his two-night Malaysian engagement at Idea Live Arena in Petaling Jaya tonight.
 The Emmy-winning comedian performed his first show yesterday, with tonight’s 8pm performance added after the original November 9 date sold out.
 Both shows have since sold out, according to organiser LOL Asia. 
 Noah, who hosted The Daily Show from 2015 to 2022, built his international reputation on sharp political satire, cultural observations and his ability to turn serious subjects into comedy.
 His Malaysian performances form part of his 2026 Asia tour, which also included sold-out dates in Singapore and Hong Kong. 
 The comedian is also a bestselling author, with his memoir Born a Crime , about growing up under apartheid in South Africa, becoming an international hit.
